links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy, evidence consistency, completeness and safety of chatbot psoriasis responses (max 8)
links.effect: Mean scores 7.36±0.97 (ChatGPT), 7.77±0.77 (Gemini), 7.05±1.09 (Copilot); differed significantly (Friedman P<0.001); all models showed high clinical safety but incomplete responses.
links.quote: The observation that models may provide accurate yet clinically incomplete responses, particularly for treatment content, emphasizes the need for physician oversight when AI-generated information is used in dermatological practice.

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks and compares the accuracy, completeness, and safety of three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) on psoriasis-related clinical and patient questions evaluated by expert dermatologists, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
